info.name: EDP Trade Process API V6
info.description:
All 40 V6 steps in workflow order, variable-chained, runnable end to end.

SAFE BY DEFAULT. Every request whose name contains [WRITE] mints, uploads, mutates or triggers. Those requests skip themselves unless the collection variable allow_writes is set to the string "true". With allow_writes left alone the run exercises 25 read-only steps against live CBOS and changes nothing.

The 'Conformance probes' folder asserts things about the V6 DOCUMENT rather than about the pipeline: they are expected to pass, and each passing probe is a defect in the doc or in a service that follows it.

exec: // Skip any request tagged as a write when allow_writes is not "true".
// pm.variables resolves the whole scope chain (environment beats collection),
// so an environment file can turn writes on without editing the collection.
// Runs after every request. The conformance probes assert their own status
// codes (Probe A expects a 400), so the blanket check skips them.

request.description: The billing engine uses this same call as the DMSTMT *trigger*, not just a poll - the one post-trade process whose trigger is a status endpoint.

Live response carries Description, ExchangeCodeUsed, DateBasis, MatchType, Trading_Date_DDMMYYYY and LastTradingDate_DDMMYYYY - none of them documented in V6. DateBasis (T-1) is the field that tells you which date belongs in the filename.

item.name: Conformance probes (assert the doc is wrong)
Probe A - Shape B without Segment must 400

exec: pm.test("V6 Shape B does not exist: CBOS rejects a payload with no Segment", function () {

request.description: The V6 doc defines Shape B for Steps 14, 16-17, 20-21, 23-24, 29, 31-32, 38-39. This probe proves Shape B is rejected outright. Every one of those steps needs Segment.

item.name: Probe B - post-trade pseudo segment codes are rejected

exec: pm.test("Segment=COLVAL is INVALID SEGMENT (the billing engine sends this)", function () { pm.expect(msg.toUpperCase()).to.eql("INVALID SEGMENT"); });

request.description: cams-edp-billing-automation-agent-repo sends the pseudo segment_code (COLVAL, COLALLOC, MTFFT, DMRPT, DMSTMT) in the Segment field of every post-trade GTG poll. CBOS answers INVALID SEGMENT, which is not TRUE, so those polls can never pass.

item.name: Probe C - DailyMarginReporting is not a known ProcessName

exec: pm.test("DailyMarginReporting is rejected as a ProcessName", function () { pm.expect(msg.toUpperCase()).to.eql("INVALID PROCESS NAME"); });

request.description: POST_TRADE_GTG_PROCESS_NAME maps DMRPT to 'DailyMarginReporting'. The V6 doc never defines a GTG ProcessName for Daily Margin Reporting (Steps 36-37 are CombinedMarginProcess only), and CBOS does not know this one.
